propositions: A Jira parent removal is never reflected locally because the fetcher omits the parent field entirely when parent_map returns None, making a de-parented issue indistinguishable from one never parented
The inbound differ refuses to emit parent_id=None to avoid clearing a locally-set parent that could not yet resolve, but this conflates two distinct cases: truly absent parent versus unresolvable key

The differ's managed_refs gate cannot distinguish whether rebar ever pushed a parent to the peer; it only answers whether the ref was set locally, leaving a gap when outbound never emitted the parent (the normal case on both backends)

Clearing a parent without positive evidence that the peer once had it caused a production incident destroying 63 parent edges on Cloud, because the same-pass suppression is structurally unreachable for non-epic parents

The fix requires per-binding peer-state tracking via ADR-0026 baseline: record the last-observed parent only when the parent key is present in a snapshot, then clear only when evidence shows the peer once carried this parent
On the first passes after the fix lands, no binding carries a recorded observation, so no parent clears are emitted; the feature self-heals into correctness as passes accumulate evidence
